# Week 1

## Lecture 1: Introduction to IoT- Part-I (Lecture 1)

### Q1. What is the primary vision of the Internet of Things (IoT)? `[Easy]`

- A. Connecting only computers and computing devices globally.
- B. Expanding the internet to interconnect all physical objects around us.
- C. Developing new software for existing internet services.
- D. Creating a separate network exclusively for mobile phones.

> **Answer**: `B. Expanding the internet to interconnect all physical objects around us.`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The transcript states, 'what Internet of Things says is that the scope of this internet is going to be expanded so it is going to be expanded beyond computing and computer devices being connected it is going to interconnect different things that physical objects that we see around us.'

### Q2. Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a physical object that could be interconnected in an IoT system? `[Easy]`

- A. A toothbrush
- B. A microwave oven
- C. A refrigerator
- D. A traditional landline phone

> **Answer**: `D. A traditional landline phone`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The transcript lists 'the lighting system in a room the lights the fans the air conditioners and anything and everything including things such as the toothbrush the microwave oven the refrigerator and so on and so forth.' A traditional landline phone is not mentioned.

### Q3. How are physical objects envisioned to become part of the Internet of Things? `[Easy]`

- A. By being replaced with entirely new digital versions.
- B. By being fitted with embedded systems, electronics, and information technology.
- C. By connecting them directly to the existing electrical grid.
- D. By manually inputting their data into a central server.

> **Answer**: `B. By being fitted with embedded systems, electronics, and information technology.`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The transcript states, 'all of these are going to be fitted with embedded systems embedded electronics and information technology so that they have some basic computing platform in them attached to them.'

### Q4. How does the scope of the Internet of Things compare to the current internet of computers? `[Easy]`

- A. IoT is expected to be smaller, focusing on niche applications.
- B. IoT is expected to be much bigger, connecting billions and trillions of things.
- C. IoT will replace the current internet entirely.
- D. IoT will only connect devices within a single household.

> **Answer**: `B. IoT is expected to be much bigger, connecting billions and trillions of things.`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The transcript mentions, 'a big internet is going to be formed which is much much bigger than the current internet of computers' and 'billions and in fact billions and trillions of things are going to be connected to the internetwork of things.'

### Q5. What are the two main approaches discussed for building the Internet of Things? `[Medium]`

- A. Expanding the current internet or building a separate internetwork from scratch.
- B. Using only wired connections or only wireless connections.

- D. Developing new hardware or new software.

> **Answer**: `A. Expanding the current internet or building a separate internetwork from scratch.`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The transcript states, 'this internetwork of things can be construed to be built in two different ways one way is to expend the scope of the current internet... The other approach is to build a separate internetwork of these physical objects from scratch.'

> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The transcript states, 'each of these nodes are typically very low power they have very low resources and they have to ah ah they have to be you know whenever they are not required they have to be put to the sleeping mode they have to go ah through a sleep cycle.'

## Lecture 2: Introduction to IoT- Part-II (Lecture 2)

### Q1. What is a fundamental problem expected to arise with the vast number of interconnected IoT devices? `[Easy]`

- A) Power consumption issues
- B) Address crunch
- C) Data storage limitations
- D) Processing power deficits

> **Answer**: `B) Address crunch`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The transcript states, 'one fundamental problem that is going to be happen is there is going to be an address crunch.'

### Q2. According to one study mentioned, how many devices were estimated to be internetworked by 2018? `[Easy]`

- A) 5 to 10 billion
- B) 10 to 20 billion
- C) 20 to 50 billion
- D) 50 to 100 billion

> **Answer**: `C) 20 to 50 billion`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The transcript mentions, 'it is estimated as per one of the studies that by two thousand eighteen almost we are going to be have twenty to fifty billion devices that are connected.'

### Q3. Why is IPv4 considered insufficient for the future of IoT addressing? `[Medium]`

- A) It lacks security features.
- B) Its 32-bit address length provides an insufficient address space.
- C) It is too complex for IoT devices.
- D) It does not support wireless communication.

> **Answer**: `B) Its 32-bit address length provides an insufficient address space.`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The transcript states, 'ipv four is defiantly not good enough... the number of addresses in ipv four is s two the power thirty two only.' This implies the address space is the issue.

### Q4. What is identified as a challenge regarding the diverse connectivity mechanisms available for IoT? `[Medium]`

- A) High cost of implementation
- B) Lack of standardized hardware
- C) Need for handshaking between different isolated standards
- D) Limited bandwidth availability

> **Answer**: `C) Need for handshaking between different isolated standards`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The transcript says, 'this is going to be another challenge with respect to network so how you are going to have some kind of a handshaking between each of this different isolated standards.'

### Q5. What is the primary characteristic of an IoT LAN? `[Easy]`

- A) Interconnecting geographically dispersed networks.
- B) Providing global internet connectivity.

### Q6. What is the function of an IoT WAN? `[Easy]`

- A) To connect individual IoT nodes directly to the internet.
- B) To provide local, short-range communication within a building.

### Q7. What is the primary role of an IoT Gateway? `[Medium]`

- A) To provide local unique addresses to devices within a LAN.
- B) To connect an IoT LAN to the WAN or the outside world.

## Lecture 4: Actuation (Lecture 4)

### Q1. What is the primary function of an actuator based on sensor readings? `[Easy]`

- A) Sense environmental parameters
- B) Store energy
- C) Perform actions on the environment or a system
- D) Generate control signals

> **Answer**: `C) Perform actions on the environment or a system`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: Based on the readings of the sensor, some action might be required to be taken and that is done by actuators. These actuators basically perform certain actions on the environment, on another system, on a device.

### Q2. Actuators typically convert a control signal and energy into what primary output? `[Easy]`

- A) Thermal energy
- B) Electrical signal
- C) Mechanical motion
- D) Potential energy

> **Answer**: `C) Mechanical motion`

> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: When these actuators receive a control signal they respond by converting that energy into mechanical motion.

# Week 2

## Lecture 6: Basics of IoT Networking-Part II (Lecture 6)

### Q1. What is the full form of MQTT? `[Easy]`

- A) Message Queue Telemetry Transport
- B) Message Query Transmission Protocol
- C) Mobile Queue Transfer Technology
- D) Machine Query Telemetry Tool

> **Answer**: `A) Message Queue Telemetry Transport`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The full form of MQTT is Message Queue Telemetry Transport, as explicitly stated in the lecture.

### Q2. MQTT is based on which communication model? `[Easy]`

- A) Request-response model
- B) Client-server model
- C) Publish-subscribe model
- D) Peer-to-peer model

> **Answer**: `C) Publish-subscribe model`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: MQTT is an ISO standard which is based on the publish-subscribe model.

### Q3. When was MQTT first introduced and by which company? `[Medium]`

- A) 2013 by OASIS
- B) 1999 by IBM
- C) 2005 by Microsoft
- D) 1995 by Cisco

> **Answer**: `B) 1999 by IBM`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: MQTT was introduced in 1999 by IBM and later standardized in 2013 by OASIS.

### Q4. Which of the following is NOT one of the three core concepts involved in MQTT? `[Medium]`

- A) Message Broker
- B) Topic
- C) Client
- D) Server

> **Answer**: `D) Server`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The three core concepts involved in MQTT are the message broker, topic, and client (publishers/subscribers). 'Server' is not listed as a distinct core concept in this context.

### Q5. A key advantage of MQTT, especially for IoT devices, is its: `[Easy]`

- A) High bandwidth requirement
- B) Large code footprint
- C) Small code footprint
- D) Complex configuration

> **Answer**: `C) Small code footprint`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: MQTT provides a very small code footprint, making it suitable for remote connections and limited bandwidth environments.

### Q6. In MQTT, which component is responsible for classifying sensor data into different topics and connecting publishers and subscribers? `[Easy]`

- A) Publisher
- B) Subscriber
- C) Broker
- D) Sensor

> **Answer**: `C) Broker`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The broker helps the publishers and the subscribers connect to one another and also helps in classifying the sensor data into different topics.

### Q7. Which MQTT method is used to establish a connection with the server? `[Easy]`

- A) Publish
- B) Subscribe
- C) Connect
- D) Disconnect

> **Answer**: `C) Connect`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The `connect` method helps to connect with the server.

### Q8. The communication architecture followed by MQTT is primarily: `[Easy]`

- A) Request-response
- B) Client-server
- C) Publish-subscribe
- D) Peer-to-peer

> **Answer**: `C) Publish-subscribe`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The communication architecture that is followed is the publish-subscribe architecture, and not the request-response architecture that is typically followed by traditional HTTP.

### Q9. Which of the following is a valid example of an MQTT topic for temperature data in a living room within a smart house? `[Medium]`

- A) house/living_room/temperature
- B) temperature.living_room.house
- C) living_room_temperature_house
- D) house:living_room:temperature

> **Answer**: `A) house/living_room/temperature`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: MQTT topics use hierarchical levels separated by a slash, as shown in the example `house/living_room/temperature`.

### Q10. In MQTT, which character represents a single-level wildcard in a topic subscription? `[Medium]`

- A) #
- B) *
- C) +
- D) ?

> **Answer**: `C) +`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The plus sign (+) is a wildcard character which only allows arbitrary values for one hierarchy.

### Q11. To subscribe to all topics beginning with 'house' (e.g., house/living_room/temperature, house/kitchen/humidity), which multi-level wildcard topic would be used? `[Medium]`

- A) house/+
- B) house/*
- C) house/#
- D) house/?

> **Answer**: `C) house/#`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The hash sign (#) is a multilevel wildcard; it allows to subscribe to all underlying hierarchical levels, for example, `house/#` is for subscribing to all topics beginning with house.

### Q12. The publish-subscribe model in MQTT is described as being: `[Easy]`

- A) Polling-based
- B) Request-driven
- C) Event-driven
- D) Batch-processed

> **Answer**: `C) Event-driven`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: This publish-subscribe model is event-driven, meaning whenever there is an event, those data are basically pushed to the clients.

### Q17. How does MQTT's communication architecture fundamentally differ from traditional HTTP? `[Medium]`

> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: MQTT follows a publish-subscribe architecture, which is event-driven, unlike the request-response architecture that is typically followed by traditional HTTP.

> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The lecture states, 'this is not unique classification in anyway and it can be it should be constitute in that manner.'

### Q47. What is required at the subscriber end for decryption in SMQTT? `[Medium]`

- A) A public key.
- B) A session key.
- C) The same master secret key used for encryption.
- D) A different master secret key.

> **Answer**: `C) The same master secret key used for encryption.`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The data is finally decrypted at the subscriber end having the same master secret key.

### Q48. The lightweight nature of MQTT makes it suitable for: `[Easy]`

- A) High-definition video streaming.
- B) Devices with abundant processing power.
- C) Resource-constrained IoT devices.
- D) Enterprise-level database synchronization.

> **Answer**: `C) Resource-constrained IoT devices.`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: MQTT's lightweight nature and small code footprint make it ideal for resource-constrained IoT devices operating in limited bandwidth environments.

### Q49. In the MQTT publish-subscribe model, what do clients primarily need to communicate over? `[Medium]`

- A) Each other's network addresses.
- B) A shared topic.
- C) Direct peer-to-peer connections.
- D) A central server's IP address.

> **Answer**: `B) A shared topic.`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: Clients do not have to know each other; they only need to communicate with each other over the topic.

### Q50. SMQTT is best described as: `[Easy]`

- A) A completely new protocol replacing MQTT.
- B) A subset of MQTT functionalities.
- C) An extension of MQTT with added security features.
- D) A different protocol for non-IoT applications.

> **Answer**: `C) An extension of MQTT with added security features.`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: Secure MQTT is an extension of MQTT, using different security features such as encryption.

## Lecture 7: Basics of IoT Networking-Part- III (Lecture 7)

### Q1. What is the primary purpose of the CoAP protocol in the context of IoT? `[Easy]`

- A) High-bandwidth video streaming
- B) Web transfer in resource-constrained networks
- C) Secure financial transactions
- D) Real-time operating system management

> **Answer**: `B) Web transfer in resource-constrained networks`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: CoAP is particularly used for web transfer in the context of constrained networks with limited resources.

### Q2. CoAP is often considered an equivalent to which standard web protocol for IoT environments? `[Easy]`

- A) FTP
- B) SMTP
- C) HTTP
- D) SSH

> **Answer**: `C) HTTP`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: CoAP is described as an HTTP equivalent that can be used in the context of IoT.

### Q3. Which layer of the OSI model does CoAP primarily operate at, or can be considered part of? `[Medium]`

- A) Network layer
- B) Transport layer
- C) Session layer
- D) Data Link layer

> **Answer**: `C) Session layer`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: CoAP is strictly speaking a session layer protocol, though it can also be considered an application layer protocol.

### Q4. What transport layer protocol does CoAP work on top of? `[Easy]`

- A) TCP
- B) SCTP
- C) UDP
- D) ICMP

> **Answer**: `C) UDP`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: CoAP works on top of UDP, which is a transport layer protocol.

### Q5. Which working group proposed the CoAP protocol? `[Medium]`

- A) IEEE 802.15.4
- B) IETF RESTful environment
- C) W3C
- D) ISO

> **Answer**: `B) IETF RESTful environment`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: CoAP is based on the IETF RESTful environment working group.

### Q6. What are the two main sub-layers of CoAP architecture? `[Medium]`

- A) Security and Presentation
- B) Messaging and Request-Response
- C) Data Link and Network
- D) Physical and Transport

> **Answer**: `B) Messaging and Request-Response`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: CoAP has two main sub-layers: the messaging sub-layer and the request-response sub-layer.

### Q7. What is the primary responsibility of the messaging sub-layer in CoAP? `[Medium]`

- A) Encoding data for transmission
- B) Ensuring reliability and avoiding message duplication
- C) Routing messages across networks
- D) Managing session establishment

> **Answer**: `B) Ensuring reliability and avoiding message duplication`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The messaging sub-layer is responsible for functionality such as reliability and avoidance of duplication of messages.

### Q8. In the CoAP confirmable message mode, what does the client expect after sending a message? `[Easy]`

- A) A separate data response
- B) No response
- C) An acknowledgement
- D) A connection reset

> **Answer**: `C) An acknowledgement`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: In a confirmable message, a message is sent and an acknowledgement is received.

### Q9. Which CoAP message mode involves the server sending its response directly along with the acknowledgement? `[Medium]`

- A) Confirmable
- B) Non-confirmable
- C) Piggyback
- D) Separate

> **Answer**: `C) Piggyback`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: In the piggyback mode, along with the acknowledgement message, the data (response) is also sent.

### Q10. What happens in the CoAP separate message mode? `[Medium]`

- A) No acknowledgement is sent
- B) The response is sent immediately with the acknowledgement
- C) An acknowledgement is received, and the response is sent separately later
- D) The client sends multiple requests without waiting for responses

> **Answer**: `C) An acknowledgement is received, and the response is sent separately later`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: In the separate mode, the server response comes in a message separate from the acknowledgement, which may take some time.

### Q11. Which CoAP functionality is used for the retrieval of data? `[Easy]`

- A) PUT
- B) PUSH
- C) GET
- D) DELETE

> **Answer**: `C) GET`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: GET is for retrieval of some data.

### Q12. Which CoAP functionality is used for creating or putting data into a repository? `[Easy]`

- A) GET
- B) PUT
- C) PUSH
- D) DELETE

> **Answer**: `B) PUT`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: PUT is for creation, or to put some data into the repository or server.

### Q13. Why is CoAP considered more suitable than REST for constrained IoT environments? `[Medium]`

- A) CoAP uses TCP, which is more reliable
- B) CoAP is a lightweight equivalent that consumes fewer resources
- C) REST does not support client-server architecture
- D) CoAP offers higher bandwidth

> **Answer**: `B) CoAP is a lightweight equivalent that consumes fewer resources`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: REST is quite resource-hungry and not good for constrained environments, whereas CoAP is a lightweight equivalent that helps communicate under low power constraints.

### Q14. What is a characteristic of the CoAP non-confirmable message mode? `[Easy]`

- A) It requires a retransmission timer
- B) It guarantees delivery
- C) There is no acknowledgement from the server
- D) It is used for critical data

> **Answer**: `C) There is no acknowledgement from the server`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: For non-confirmable messages, there is no acknowledgement from the server.

### Q15. What is the role of the request-response sub-layer in CoAP? `[Medium]`

- A) Managing network security
- B) Handling the exact communication of sending a request and receiving a response
- C) Compressing data for transmission
- D) Discovering network resources

> **Answer**: `B) Handling the exact communication of sending a request and receiving a response`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The request-response sub-layer is responsible for the exact communication that is going to take place, the request being sent and the response being received.

### Q16. CoAP helps to reduce which two aspects of network communication? `[Medium]`

- A) Latency and throughput
- B) Overhead and parsing complexity
- C) Security and encryption
- D) Bandwidth and reliability

> **Answer**: `B) Overhead and parsing complexity`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: CoAP and its different message types help to induce the overhead and the parsing complexity of the network.

### Q17. In the context of CoAP, what does 'constrained' refer to? `[Easy]`

- A) Limited number of network devices
- B) Limited energy, computational, and communication resources
- C) Restricted geographical area
- D) Specific data types only

> **Answer**: `B) Limited energy, computational, and communication resources`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: Constrained networks refer to nodes constrained with respect to different resources such as limited energy/power supply, computational resources, communication resources, and bandwidth.

### Q18. Which CoAP functionality is used for updating existing data? `[Medium]`

- A) GET
- B) PUT
- C) PUSH
- D) DELETE

> **Answer**: `C) PUSH`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: For updating, the PUSH message is used.

### Q19. What kind of interaction model does CoAP follow? `[Easy]`

- A) Peer-to-peer
- B) Broadcast
- C) Client-server
- D) Multicast

> **Answer**: `C) Client-server`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: CoAP involves a client-server kind of interaction.

### Q20. What is a key difference between CoAP and HTTP regarding resource usage? `[Medium]`

- A) HTTP is lightweight, CoAP is heavy
- B) CoAP is resource-hungry, HTTP is not
- C) CoAP is designed for resource-constrained environments, HTTP is not
- D) Both are equally resource-efficient

> **Answer**: `C) CoAP is designed for resource-constrained environments, HTTP is not`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: REST (and by extension HTTP) is quite resource hungry, whereas CoAP is a lightweight equivalent for constrained environments.

### Q21. What does XMPP stand for? `[Easy]`

- A) Extensible Markup Protocol for Presence
- B) eXtended Message Processing Protocol
- C) Extensible Messaging and Presence Protocol
- D) XML Message Packet Protocol

> **Answer**: `C) Extensible Messaging and Presence Protocol`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The full form of XMPP is Extensible Messaging and Presence Protocol.

### Q22. XMPP is a message-oriented middleware based on which markup language? `[Easy]`

- A) HTML
- B) JSON
- C) XML
- D) YAML

> **Answer**: `C) XML`
>

### Q23. What type of data exchange is XMPP particularly useful for? `[Medium]`

- A) Unstructured data archiving

>

>

## Lecture 8: Basics of IoT Networking- Part-IV (Lecture 8)

### Q1. What does AMQP stand for? `[Easy]`

- Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
- Asynchronous Message Query Protocol
- Automated Message Quality Protocol
- Application Message Queueing Process

> **Answer**: `Advanced Message Queuing Protocol`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The full form of AMQP is Advanced Message Queuing Protocol, as stated in the lecture.

### Q2. AMQP follows an open standard based on which organization? `[Easy]`

- ISO/IEC
- IEEE
- IETF
- W3C

> **Answer**: `ISO/IEC`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: AMQP follows an open standard based on the ISO/IEC 19464 standard.

### Q3. The primary purpose of the ISO/IEC 19464 standard, as applied to AMQP, is to define how: `[Medium]`

- Network packets are routed across the internet
- Messages are passed between business applications and organizations
- Electrical signals are transmitted over physical media
- Data is encrypted for secure communication

> **Answer**: `Messages are passed between business applications and organizations`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The standard helps define how messages are going to be passed from businesses, business applications, or organizations, facilitating communication between different systems and processes.

### Q4. AMQP is classified as which type of protocol? `[Easy]`

- Data Link Layer
- Network Layer
- Transport Layer
- Application Layer

> **Answer**: `Application Layer`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The lecture states that AMQP is a binary application layer protocol.

### Q5. In AMQP, the unit used for data transfer is known as a: `[Medium]`

- Packet
- Segment
- Datagram
- Frame

> **Answer**: `Frame`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The unit used for data transfer in AMQP is known as the frame, which is distinct from the link layer frame.

### Q6. In the AMQP architecture, the server primarily acts as a: `[Medium]`

- Client
- Producer
- Consumer
- Broker

> **Answer**: `Broker`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The server in the AMQP architecture acts as a broker, comprising routers, filters, and queues.

### Q7. Which of the following correctly represents the flow of messages in AMQP? `[Medium]`

- Consumer -> Server -> Producer
- Producer -> Server -> Consumer
- Server -> Producer -> Consumer
- Producer -> Consumer -> Server

> **Answer**: `Producer -> Server -> Consumer`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: Messages are sent from producers to the server (broker) and then forwarded to consumers.

### Q8. AMQP's general features include connecting distinct entities across which dimensions? `[Hard]`

- Hardware, Software, Firmware
- Organizations, Technologies, Time, and Space
- Clients, Servers, and Databases
- Protocols, Algorithms, and Devices

> **Answer**: `Organizations, Technologies, Time, and Space`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: AMQP helps in connecting different organizations, technologies, at different points of time, and in different locations (space).

### Q9. Which of the following is NOT explicitly mentioned as a specific feature of AMQP from a different perspective? `[Medium]`

- Security
- Reliability
- Interoperability
- Data Compression

> **Answer**: `Data Compression`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The lecture mentions security, reliability, and interoperability as specific features, but not data compression.

### Q10. AMQP's interoperability refers to the interoperability of: `[Medium]`

- Only devices
- Only protocols
- Only algorithms
- Devices, protocols, algorithms, and messages

> **Answer**: `Devices, protocols, algorithms, and messages`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: Interoperability in AMQP refers to not only devices but also protocols, algorithms, messages, and so on.

### Q11. Which message delivery guarantee ensures that a message is delivered at most once (once or never)? `[Easy]`

- At least once
- Exactly once
- At most once
- Never once

> **Answer**: `At most once`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: 'At most once' means each message is delivered at most once, i.e., once or never.

### Q12. Which message delivery guarantee ensures that a message is certain to be delivered, but may do so multiple times? `[Easy]`

- At least once
- Exactly once
- At most once
- Only once

> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: 'At least once' means each message is certain to be delivered but may do so multiple times.

- At least once
- Exactly once
- At most once
- Multiple times

> **Answer**: `Exactly once`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: 'Exactly once' means messages will always certainly arrive and do so only once.

- Opening a connection

- Flow

>

>

>

### Q19. The 'Begin' frame type in AMQP is used for: `[Medium]`

- Opening a connection
- Opening a session
- Initiating a new link transfer

## Lecture 9: Connectivity Technologies- Part-I (Lecture 9)

### Q1. Which IEEE standard is primarily used for forming Wireless Personal Area Networks (WPANs) with low data rates and low power consumption? `[Easy]`

- IEEE 802.11
- IEEE 802.3
- IEEE 802.15.4
- IEEE 802.16

> **Answer**: `IEEE 802.15.4`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The lecture states that IEEE 802.15.4 is used for forming wireless personal area networks, which are typically low data rate and low power consuming.

### Q2. The IEEE 802.15.4 standard primarily focuses on which layers of the OSI model? `[Easy]`

- Application and Presentation
- Network and Transport
- Physical and MAC
- Session and Data Link

> **Answer**: `Physical and MAC`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The standard focuses on primarily the two layers which are the physical and MAC.

### Q3. What modulation scheme is primarily used by IEEE 802.15.4 for its high tolerance to noise and interference? `[Medium]`

- OFDM
- DSSS
- FHSS
- QAM

> **Answer**: `DSSS`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: IEEE 802.15.4 is based on the modulation scheme known as DSSS (Direct Sequence Spread Spectrum technique), which is highly tolerant of noise and interference.

### Q4. Which channel access mechanism is employed by IEEE 802.15.4 for MAC communication? `[Medium]`

- TDMA
- FDMA
- CSMA/CA
- ALOHA

> **Answer**: `CSMA/CA`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: For MAC communication, it uses CSMA/CA (Carrier Sense Multiple Access with Collision Avoidance) for channel access.

### Q5. How does IEEE 802.15.4 minimize power consumption? `[Medium]`

- By using high-power amplifiers
- Through continuous data transmission
- Due to infrequently occurring very short transmissions with low duty cycle
- By operating at high data rates

> **Answer**: `Due to infrequently occurring very short transmissions with low duty cycle`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: Power consumption using this particular protocol is minimized due to the infrequently occurring very short transmissions with low duty cycle, which is less than one percent.

### Q6. Which type of device in an IEEE 802.15.4 network has reduced functionality, lower power consumption, and minimal CPU/RAM, only able to send and receive data? `[Easy]`

- PAN Coordinator
- Router
- Fully Functional Device (FFD)
- Reduced Functional Device (RFD)

> **Answer**: `Reduced Functional Device (RFD)`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The Reduced Functional Device (RFD) can only send and receive, has lower power consumption, and uses minimal CPU and RAM.

### Q7. Which of the following is NOT a capability of a Fully Functional Device (FFD) in an IEEE 802.15.4 network? `[Medium]`

- Acting as a PAN coordinator
- Acting as a router
- Undertaking all different types of functionalities
- Only sending and receiving very simple data

> **Answer**: `Only sending and receiving very simple data`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: FFDs can undertake all different types of functionalities, whereas RFDs can only do very simple things like sending and receiving.

### Q8. Which of the following is NOT one of the five defined frame types for IEEE 802.15.4? `[Easy]`

- Data frame
- Acknowledgement frame
- Routing frame
- Beacon frame

> **Answer**: `Routing frame`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The five frame types are Data, Acknowledgement, Command, MAC, and Beacon frames. Routing frame is not listed.

### Q9. What is the primary purpose of a beacon frame in an IEEE 802.15.4 network? `[Medium]`

- To carry user data
- To acknowledge received packets
- To advertise the presence of a PAN coordinator
- To send control commands for device association

> **Answer**: `To advertise the presence of a PAN coordinator`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: Beacon frames are sent by the PAN coordinator at regular intervals to advertise its presence, allowing devices to discover it.

### Q10. In a beacon-enabled IEEE 802.15.4 network, how are data frames typically sent? `[Medium]`

- Via unslotted CSMA/CA
- Via slotted CSMA/CA with a superframe structure
- Using TDMA
- Using FDMA

> **Answer**: `Via slotted CSMA/CA with a superframe structure`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: In beacon-enabled networks, data frames are sent via slotted CSMA/CA with a superframe structure that is managed by the PAN coordinator.

### Q11. What is a characteristic of a non-beacon-enabled IEEE 802.15.4 network? `[Medium]`

- Periodically transmits beacon messages
- Uses slotted CSMA/CA for data frames
- Beacons are used only for link layer discovery
- Managed by a superframe structure

> **Answer**: `Beacons are used only for link layer discovery`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: In non-beacon-enabled networks, beacons are used only for link layer discovery. Data frames are sent via unslotted CSMA/CA.

### Q22. What is a key advantage of using mesh topology in Zigbee networks? `[Medium]`

### Q23. What does 'self-healing' refer to in the context of Zigbee mesh networks? `[Medium]`

### Q28. How does the AODV protocol find a destination in a network? `[Medium]`

> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The AODV protocol broadcasts a route message to all its intermediate neighbors, these neighbors basically they relay the same information to their neighbors in turn and eventually this message spreads across throughout the network.

## Lecture 10: Connectivity Technologies- Part-II (Lecture 10)

### Q1. What does the 'six' in 6LoWPAN primarily refer to? `[Easy]`

- A) Six layers of the OSI model
- B) IPv6
- C) Six different radio frequencies
- D) Six types of low-power devices

> **Answer**: `B) IPv6`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The 'six' in 6LoWPAN comes from IPv6, as the protocol runs over IPv6.

### Q2. What is the full form of 6LoWPAN? `[Easy]`

- A) Low Power Wireless Personal Area Network over IPv6
- B) Low Power Wide Area Network over IPv6
- C) Low Power Wireless Protocol for Area Networks
- D) Low Power Wireless Personal Area Network for IoT

> **Answer**: `A) Low Power Wireless Personal Area Network over IPv6`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: 6LoWPAN stands for 'Low Power Wireless Personal Area Network over IPv6'.

### Q3. 6LoWPAN allows which type of devices to transmit information wirelessly over the Internet Protocol? `[Easy]`

- A) High-power servers
- B) Devices with unlimited processing ability
- C) Smallest devices with limited processing ability
- D) Devices requiring high bandwidth

> **Answer**: `C) Smallest devices with limited processing ability`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: 6LoWPAN allows for the smallest devices and each of these devices having limited processing ability to transmit information wirelessly over the internet protocol.

### Q4. Which IEEE standard radio is primarily used by 6LoWPAN? `[Easy]`

- A) IEEE 802.11
- B) IEEE 802.3
- C) IEEE 802.15.4
- D) IEEE 802.16

> **Answer**: `C) IEEE 802.15.4`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: 6LoWPAN allows IEEE 802.15.4 radios to carry 128-bit addresses of IPv6.

### Q5. How does 6LoWPAN enable 802.15.4 radios to access the internet using IPv6, given that 802.15.4 is lightweight and IPv6 is not? `[Medium]`

- A) By increasing the power of 802.15.4 radios
- B) Through header compression and address translation techniques
- C) By using a different addressing scheme than IPv6
- D) By bypassing the IPv6 protocol entirely

> **Answer**: `B) Through header compression and address translation techniques`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: It is made possible with the help of header compression and address translation techniques that basically helps to convert 802.15.4 radios to access the internet.

### Q6. What happens to IPv6 packets in 6LoWPAN to fit the 802.15.4 packet structure? `[Medium]`

- A) They are expanded and encrypted
- B) They are compressed and reformatted
- C) They are fragmented without compression
- D) They are directly transmitted without modification

> **Answer**: `B) They are compressed and reformatted`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: IPv6 packets are compressed and reformatted to fit the 802.15.4 packet structure.

### Q7. What are the two types of addresses used for addressing in 6LoWPAN? `[Medium]`

- A) 32-bit and 128-bit addresses
- B) 16-bit short and 64-bit extended addresses
- C) MAC addresses and IP addresses
- D) Local and global addresses

> **Answer**: `B) 16-bit short and 64-bit extended addresses`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: There are two types of addresses that are used: 16-bit short address for PAN specific communication and 64-bit extended address for global unique connectivity.

### Q8. For what purpose is the 16-bit short address used in 6LoWPAN? `[Easy]`

- A) Global unique addressing
- B) PAN specific communication
- C) Internet routing
- D) MAC layer identification

> **Answer**: `B) PAN specific communication`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The 16-bit short address is for PAN specific communication, assigned by the PAN coordinator.

### Q9. Is IPv6 multicast supported by 802.15.4 in 6LoWPAN? `[Medium]`

- A) Yes, directly
- B) Yes, with special encapsulation
- C) No, it is not supported
- D) Only for specific applications

> **Answer**: `C) No, it is not supported`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: IPv6 multicast is not supported by 802.15.4. IPv6 packets are carried as link layer broadcast frames.

### Q10. The 6LoWPAN packet format combines which two main protocol elements? `[Easy]`

- A) TCP and UDP
- B) Ethernet and Wi-Fi
- C) 802.15.4 radio and IPv6
- D) Bluetooth and Zigbee

> **Answer**: `C) 802.15.4 radio and IPv6`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The packet format shows 802.15.4 and IPv6 clubbed together, with 802.15.4 radio and IPv6 for addressing over the internet.

### Q11. Which of the following is NOT one of the three different types of headers in 6LoWPAN? `[Medium]`

- A) Dispatch header
- B) Mesh addressing header
- C) Transport header
- D) Fragmentation header

> **Answer**: `C) Transport header`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: There are three different types of headers: Dispatch header, Mesh addressing header, and Fragmentation header.

### Q12. What is the primary function of the dispatch header in 6LoWPAN? `[Medium]`

- A) To manage fragmentation of packets
- B) To identify the dispatch type and next header type
- C) To store mesh addressing information
- D) To indicate the number of hops left

> **Answer**: `B) To identify the dispatch type and next header type`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The first two bits are used to identify the dispatch type, and the dispatch field (six bits long) identifies the next header type.

### Q13. In the mesh addressing header, what does a 'V' field value of zero indicate? `[Hard]`

- A) The destination is a 16-bit address
- B) The originator is a 64-bit extended address
- C) The originator is a 16-bit address
- D) The destination is a 64-bit address

> **Answer**: `B) The originator is a 64-bit extended address`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The V field is zero if the originator is a 64-bit extended address.

### Q14. In the mesh addressing header, what does an 'F' field value of one indicate? `[Hard]`

- A) The originator is a 64-bit extended address
- B) The destination is a 64-bit address
- C) The destination is a 16-bit address
- D) The originator is a 16-bit address

> **Answer**: `C) The destination is a 16-bit address`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The F field is zero if the destination is 64-bit address and one if it is 16-bit address.

### Q15. What happens to the 'hops left' field in the mesh addressing header as a packet traverses the network? `[Easy]`

- A) It remains constant
- B) It is incremented by each node
- C) It is decremented by each node
- D) It is reset at each hop

> **Answer**: `C) It is decremented by each node`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The hops left are decremented by each node before sending to the next hop.

### Q16. What is the main difference between the first fragment header and subsequent fragment headers in 6LoWPAN? `[Medium]`

- A) Subsequent fragments include a datagram offset
- B) The first fragment includes a datagram offset
- C) Subsequent fragments are shorter
- D) The first fragment has no header

> **Answer**: `A) Subsequent fragments include a datagram offset`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The main difference between the first fragment and the subsequent fragments is the inclusion of the datagram offset in the subsequent fragments.

### Q22. What characteristic do route request and route reply messages share in LOADng regarding sequence numbers? `[Medium]`

- A) They use random sequence numbers

>

### Q23. RPL routing protocol is based on which routing principle for lossy and low power networks? `[Medium]`

## Lecture 11:Connectivity Technologies- Part-III (Lecture 11)

### Q1. What is the full form of HART protocol? `[Easy]`

- A) High-speed Addressable Remote Transceiver

- C) Home Area Remote Technology
- D) Hybrid Access Radio Transmission

> **Answer**: `B) Highway Addressable Remote Transducer`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The full form of HART is Highway Addressable Remote Transducer protocol.

### Q2. From which IEEE standard is the HART protocol primarily derived or based upon? `[Easy]`

- B) IEEE 802.3
- C) IEEE 802.15.4
- D) IEEE 802.16

> **Answer**: `C) IEEE 802.15.4`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: HART and WirelessHART are derived from or based upon the IEEE 802.15.4 standard.

### Q3. HART protocol is specifically designed with a special focus on which type of applications? `[Easy]`

- A) Consumer IoT
- B) Vehicular networks
- C) Industrial IoT
- D) Smart home systems

> **Answer**: `C) Industrial IoT`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The special focus of HART is on industrial applications, making it suitable for Industrial IoT (IIoT).

### Q4. The main difference between HART and WirelessHART lies in which layers of the OSI model? `[Medium]`

- B) Session and Transport layers
- C) Physical, Data Link, and Network layers
- D) All layers are completely different

> **Answer**: `C) Physical, Data Link, and Network layers`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The main difference between HART and WirelessHART is in the physical, data link, and network layers. Wired HART also lacks a network layer.

### Q5. Which layer is typically absent in the wired HART protocol implementation compared to WirelessHART? `[Medium]`

- A) Physical layer
- B) Data Link layer
- C) Network layer
- D) Application layer

> **Answer**: `C) Network layer`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: Wired HART basically doesn't have support for a network layer.

### Q6. In which ISM band does the WirelessHART protocol primarily function? `[Easy]`

- A) 900 MHz
- B) 5 GHz
- C) 2.4 GHz
- D) 60 GHz

> **Answer**: `C) 2.4 GHz`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The HART protocol functions in the 2.4 GHz ISM band.

### Q7. How many channels does WirelessHART exploit in the ISM band to increase network reliability? `[Medium]`

- A) 7
- B) 15
- C) 26
- D) 32

> **Answer**: `B) 15`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: WirelessHART exploits fifteen channels of the ISM band to increase the reliability of the network.

### Q8. What concept does the Data Link layer of WirelessHART use to ensure reliable, collision-free, and deterministic communication? `[Medium]`

- A) Data packets
- B) Superframes
- C) Ethernet frames
- D) IP datagrams

> **Answer**: `B) Superframes`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The Data Link layer has a concept of something known as the super frames, which helps in ensuring reliable, collision-free, and deterministic communication.

### Q9. The Data Link layer of WirelessHART works using a protocol similar to which multiple access method? `[Medium]`

- A) CSMA/CD
- B) CSMA/CA
- C) TDMA
- D) FDMA

> **Answer**: `C) TDMA`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The Data Link layer works using a TDMA-like protocol (Time Division Multiple Access).

### Q10. Superframes in WirelessHART are grouped into time slots of what duration? `[Medium]`

- A) 1 millisecond
- B) 5 milliseconds
- C) 10 milliseconds
- D) 100 milliseconds

> **Answer**: `C) 10 milliseconds`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: Superframes are grouped into ten millisecond wide time slots.

### Q11. Which two mechanisms does the Data Link layer of WirelessHART incorporate to increase reliability and security? `[Medium]`

- A) Packet filtering and encryption
- B) Channel hopping and channel blacklisting
- C) Error correction and retransmission
- D) Flow control and congestion avoidance

> **Answer**: `B) Channel hopping and channel blacklisting`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The Data Link layer incorporates channel hopping and channel blacklisting to increase reliability and security.

### Q12. WirelessHART is based on which networking topology for communication? `[Easy]`

- A) Star networking
- B) Bus networking

## Lecture 17: Sensor Networks- Part- IV (Lecture 17)

### Q1. What is the primary objective of 'coverage' in sensor networks? `[Easy]`

- To ensure all sensor nodes are connected to each other.
- To maximize the transmission range of each sensor node.
- To deploy sensors such that no point or area in a specific terrain is left unsensed.
- To minimize the energy consumption of individual sensor nodes.

> **Answer**: `To deploy sensors such that no point or area in a specific terrain is left unsensed.`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: Coverage in sensor networks aims to deploy sensor nodes in a particular terrain in such a way that no point or none of the areas in that particular terrain are left unsensed.

### Q2. Which of the following is NOT explicitly mentioned as a type of coverage in the lecture? `[Easy]`

- Point coverage
- Area coverage
- Barrier coverage
- Energy coverage

> **Answer**: `Energy coverage`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The lecture discusses point coverage, area coverage, and barrier coverage as different types of coverage. Energy coverage is not mentioned.

### Q3. What is the relationship between coverage and connectivity if the transmission range (Rc) is greater than or equal to twice the sensing range (Rs)? `[Medium]`

- Connectivity implies coverage.
- Coverage implies connectivity.
- They are independent concepts.
- They are inversely proportional.

> **Answer**: `Coverage implies connectivity.`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: It has been shown that if the transmission range (Rc) is greater than or equal to twice the sensing range (Rs), then the problem of coverage implies the problem of connectivity.

### Q4. In the context of sensor networks, what does 'network lifetime' primarily refer to? `[Easy]`

- The total data throughput of the network.
- The time until which the network is going to survive or function.
- The maximum distance data can travel in the network.
- The number of nodes that can be supported by the network.

> **Answer**: `The time until which the network is going to survive or function.`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: Network lifetime is basically, in plain and simple terms, about how long the network is going to survive.

### Q5. What is the difference between sensing range and transmission range? `[Easy]`

- Sensing range is for communication, transmission range is for detection.
- Sensing range defines the area a node can detect, transmission range defines how far it can communicate.
- They are interchangeable terms for the same concept.
- Sensing range is always larger than transmission range.

> **Answer**: `Sensing range defines the area a node can detect, transmission range defines how far it can communicate.`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: Sensing range is the radius around a node till which it can sense, while transmission range (or communication range) is concerned about how far the node can communicate.

### Q6. Which type of sensor deployment is concerned with how to plan the trajectory of sensors to cover a region spatio-temporally? `[Medium]`

- Static sensor deployment
- Deterministic sensor deployment
- Mobile sensor deployment
- Random sensor deployment

> **Answer**: `Mobile sensor deployment`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: In mobile sensors, we have to ensure that with respect to not only space as in static sensor but also with respect to time, that means spatio-temporally, that region of interest is covered.

### Q7. What is the main characteristic of 'point coverage'? `[Medium]`

- Ensuring every point in an entire area is covered.
- Ensuring a specific set of points in an area are covered by a minimal number of sensors.

- Maximizing the overlap between sensor sensing ranges.

> **Answer**: `Ensuring a specific set of points in an area are covered by a minimal number of sensors.`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: In point coverage, we are ensuring that if there is a set of points in a particular area, those set of points are covered with minimal number of sensor nodes.

### Q8. In the context of barrier coverage, what does 'k barrier coverage' imply? `[Medium]`

> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: K barrier coverage ensures that at least k number of sensors (k can be anything greater than two) basically detect this particular intrusion.

### Q28. If a continuous region R is covered, what must be true about the crossings within R? `[Medium]`

### Q30. Why is the condition Rc >= 2 * Rs important for sensor network design? `[Hard]`

In other words, we simply have to take care of coverage and if we have ensured that coverage has been taken care of in a particular area then automatically connectivity is also taken care of.

### Q44. If a servo motor is attached to pin 12 and the code `myServo.write(0); delay(1000); myServo.write(90); delay(1000); myServo.write(180); delay(1000);` is executed in the `loop()` function, what would be the *total time* for one complete cycle of movement (from 0 to 180 and back to 0, including all delays)? `[Hard]`

- A) 3 seconds
- B) 4 seconds
- C) 5 seconds
- D) 6 seconds

> **Answer**: `B) 4 seconds`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The sequence of movements and delays in one loop iteration is: move to 0 (instant), delay 1s, move to 90 (instant), delay 1s, move to 180 (instant), delay 1s. This takes 3 seconds. For the servo to return 'back to 0' to complete the cycle, the loop would restart, initiating another `myServo.write(0); delay(1000);`. Thus, a full 0-90-180-0 cycle would involve 4 delays, totaling 4 seconds.

### Q1. What is the primary protocol used for the southbound API communication in SDN? `[Easy]`

### Q12. According to the example provided, what is the correct sequence of policy enforcement for an HTTP request in an SDN security chain? `[Hard]`

### Q15. In value-centric data forwarding under the Sensor OpenFlow Protocol, when is data forwarded? `[Medium]`

- D) When the destination node requests it.

### Q16. How does ID-centric data forwarding work in the Sensor OpenFlow Protocol? `[Medium]`

### Q1. Which of the following is a common problem encountered in traditional mobile wireless networks? `[Easy]`

### Q2. According to the Open Network Foundation, which aspect of SDN is well-suited for end-to-end communication over multiple technologies like WiFi, 3G, and 4G in mobile networks? `[Medium]`

### Q3. What is a key benefit of logically centralized control in SDN for mobile networks? `[Medium]`

### Q4. How does network virtualization contribute to SDN in mobile networks? `[Medium]`

> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: As we can see over here, we have an SDN controller, which provides centralized control and coordination for the network.

### Q33. The presence of heterogeneous devices in mobile IoT networks poses a challenge for rule placement because: `[Medium]`

> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The presence of heterogeneous devices means different types of heterogeneous devices having different configurations, supporting different vendor specific solutions and protocols, which exist in a realistic mobile based IoT network.

### Q34. What facilitates the communication between the ODIN agent and the ODIN master? `[Medium]`

- A) Direct hardware connection
- B) A handshaking process
- C) A pre-configured static table
- D) A broadcast mechanism

> **Answer**: `B) A handshaking process`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: It is this handshaking between the communication between the ODIN agent and the ODIN master that is taken care of by this ODIN protocol.

### Q35. Which of the following is an issue addressed by the mobility management part of UbiFlow? `[Medium]`

### Q36. After network partitioning in UbiFlow's flow scheduling, what is the next step when a mobile device receives a packet? `[Medium]`

- B) Network matching to determine which partition handles the packet

- D) Predicting user location

>

### Q37. MobiFlow addresses the problem of limited flow table spaces by: `[Medium]`

- A) Allowing flow tables to grow indefinitely
- B) Proactively placing rules based on user movement
- C) Using only exact match rules
- D) Eliminating the need for flow tables

> **Answer**: `B) Proactively placing rules based on user movement`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: MobiFlow gives a proactive rule placement scheme depending on the users' movement in the network, which helps manage the limited flow table spaces.

### Q38. What is the basis for MobiFlow's proactive rule placement scheme? `[Medium]`

- A) Random rule generation
- B) Prediction of end-user locations
- C) Static network configurations
- D) Manual administrator input

> **Answer**: `B) Prediction of end-user locations`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: What is very important is to have some kind of prediction of the location of the end users at the next time instant, given the data of how the user was moving till a particular time instant.

### Q39. Why is load balancing an important issue for the backbone network of IoT? `[Easy]`

- C) Dynamic resource allocation

### Q41. Before inserting flow rules at switches in SDN-enabled data centers, what is required to adequately forward data? `[Easy]`

### Q48. MobiFlow's goal for flow rules in the context of limited flow table space is to: `[Medium]`

## Lecture 37 : Cloud Computing-Fundamental (Lecture 37)

### Q1. What analogy is used to explain the concept of 'computing as a utility'? `[Easy]`

- Telephone services
- Transportation networks
- Electricity and water supply
- Postal services

> **Answer**: `Electricity and water supply`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The lecture explains cloud computing by comparing it to utilities like electricity and water, where users pay for usage without needing to manage the underlying infrastructure.

### Q2. According to NIST, which of the following is a key characteristic of cloud computing? `[Medium]`

- Dedicated hardware for each user
- On-demand network access to a shared pool of configurable computing resources
- Requirement for users to manage physical servers
- Fixed monthly subscription without usage-based billing

> **Answer**: `On-demand network access to a shared pool of configurable computing resources`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: NIST defines cloud computing as 'a model for enabling convenient on demand network access to a shared pool of configurable computing resources'.

### Q3. Which essential characteristic of cloud computing allows users to scale computing resources up or down as needed? `[Easy]`

- Broad network access
- Measured services
- Rapid elasticity
- Resource pooling

> **Answer**: `Rapid elasticity`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: Rapid elasticity means that as and when required, users can scale up or scale down computational resources dynamically.

### Q4. Which cloud service model provides consumers with the ability to deploy and run consumer-created or acquired applications using programming languages and tools supported by the provider? `[Medium]`

- Software as a Service (SaaS)
- Platform as a Service (PaaS)
- Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
- Hardware as a Service (HaaS)

> **Answer**: `Platform as a Service (PaaS)`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: PaaS makes the development platform available to consumers as facilities to execute consumer-created and acquired applications onto the cloud infrastructure.

### Q5. A cloud deployment model restricted to a single organization, typically managed by the organization itself or a third party, is known as a: `[Easy]`

- Public cloud
- Hybrid cloud
- Community cloud
- Private cloud

> **Answer**: `Private cloud`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: A private cloud is typically restricted to a single organization, and its functionalities are made available only within that organization.

### Q6. One business advantage of cloud computing is 'reduced time to market.' How does cloud computing achieve this? `[Medium]`

- By eliminating the need for software development
- By providing free computational resources
- By cutting down on time spent on procurement and deployment of computational resources
- By automating all marketing strategies

> **Answer**: `By cutting down on time spent on procurement and deployment of computational resources`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: Cloud computing reduces time to market because companies do not spend time and money on procurement, tendering, delivery, and setup of infrastructure.

### Q7. Cloud computing is described as an integration of concepts from which earlier computing models? `[Medium]`

- Mainframe computing, ARPANET, Virtual Machines

- Distributed computing, Parallel computing, Edge computing
- Client-server computing, Peer-to-peer computing, Mobile computing

### Q8. What does 'measured services' in cloud computing imply? `[Easy]`

- Users pay a fixed monthly fee regardless of usage
- Resource usage is recorded, monitored, and billed based on consumption

> **Answer**: `Resource usage is recorded, monitored, and billed based on consumption`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: Measured services mean that resources and their uses are recorded and monitored, and users are billed based on the units of utility consumed.

## Lecture 42 : Sensor-Cloud- I (Lecture 42)

### Q1. What is the primary concept behind Sensor Cloud technology? `[Easy]`

- Offering computing facilities as a service.
- Integrating sensor networks and cloud technology to offer sensing as a service.
- Storing sensor data in the cloud without further processing.
- Virtualizing computing platforms for sensor data analysis.

> **Answer**: `Integrating sensor networks and cloud technology to offer sensing as a service.`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The transcript states, 'sensor cloud as the name suggests is about integration of two technologies sensor rather sensor networks and cloud technology so the whole idea is through the integration of sensor technology or sensor network technology with cloud can we offer sensors or sensing as a service'.

### Q2. Which of the following is NOT considered a simple integration or function of Sensor Cloud, according to the lecture? `[Medium]`

- Dumping sense data to the cloud.
- Simple virtualization of sensors.
- Offering sensing as a service.
- Mere integration of sensors and cloud computing technology.

> **Answer**: `Offering sensing as a service.`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The lecture clarifies that Sensor Cloud 'is not nearly about getting the sense data to the cloud dumping the sense data to the cloud or its not about the simple virtualization of the sensors' and 'it is not a mere integration of sensors and cloud computing technology'. Offering sensing as a service is the core benefit and advanced concept.

- C) To aggregate less time-sensitive data for analysis before sending summaries to the cloud.
- D) To provide permanent storage for all data from IoT devices.

> **Answer**: `C) To aggregate less time-sensitive data for analysis before sending summaries to the cloud.`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The lecture explains, 'if the data is relative less time sensitive then it is aggregated at the fog node and that aggregated data is sent as summary for historical analysis and storage to the cloud'. This refers to the aggregate fog node.

## Lecture 50 : Connected Vehicles- II (Lecture 50)

### Q1. What does 'intelligence' in Intelligent Connected Vehicles primarily refer to? `[Easy]`

- A. The physical design of the vehicle.
- B. The implementation of various software for decision-making.
- C. The type of fuel used by the vehicle.
- D. The speed at which the vehicle can travel.

> **Answer**: `B. The implementation of various software for decision-making.`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: Intelligence in ICVs comes from the implementation of different types of software, enabling intelligent decision-making, inferences, and predictions based on collected data.

### Q2. Which of the following is NOT a primary source of data for intelligent decision-making in Connected Vehicles? `[Medium]`

- C. Real-time data from sensors.
- D. Manual input from the driver's smartphone.

> **Answer**: `D. Manual input from the driver's smartphone.`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The lecture states that data is obtained either from embedded hardware or from historical data collected from different vehicles, which includes real-time sensor data. Manual input from a driver's smartphone is not mentioned as a primary source for intelligent decision-making in this context.

# Week 11

## Lecture 51: Smart Grid- I (Lecture 51)

### Q1. What is the primary goal of making the traditional electrical grid 'smart' in the context of the Internet of Things? `[Easy]`

- A. To replace all existing power plants with renewable energy sources.
- B. To integrate advanced information and communication technologies (ICT) for efficiency and reliability.
- C. To eliminate the need for human intervention in power distribution.
- D. To centralize all energy generation and distribution systems.

> **Answer**: `B. To integrate advanced information and communication technologies (ICT) for efficiency and reliability.`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The smart grid aims to make the traditional electrical grid smart through the use of advanced information and communication technologies (ICT) to achieve higher reliability and overall system smartness.

### Q2. Which of the following best describes the communication flow in a traditional electrical grid? `[Easy]`

- A. Bidirectional, allowing consumers to send data back to the source.
- B. Unidirectional, from the source to the end consumers.
- C. Primarily wireless, using IoT sensors.
- D. Non-existent, as communication is not a feature of traditional grids.

> **Answer**: `B. Unidirectional, from the source to the end consumers.`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: In a traditional electrical grid, the communication is unidirectional, from the source to the end consumers.

### Q3. According to the lecture, what type of system is the smart grid considered to be? `[Easy]`

- A. A purely physical system.
- B. A purely cyber system.
- C. A cyber-physical system.
- D. A standalone energy generation system.

> **Answer**: `C. A cyber-physical system.`
> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: The smart grid is described as a cyber-physical system where the cyber part (internet/network) is tightly intertwined with the physical system to make it smart.

### Q4. What organization, based in the US, defined the smart grid as a modernized grid enabling bidirectional energy flow and two-way communication? `[Medium]`

> 
> **Explanation & Transcript Citation**: NIST, an organization based in the US, defined the smart grid as a modernized grid that enables bidirectional flow of energy and uses two-way communication and control capabilities.

### Q5. Which of the following is NOT a direct benefit of the smart grid mentioned in the lecture? `[Medium]`
